item.title: What to Know About Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop
item.description: The air traffic control system’s overloaded, antiquated telecommunications equipment sustained its latest widespread failure, prompting a call for more money to fuel faster upgrades.
item.dc:creator: Karoun Demirjian
item.media:description: Passengers at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport on Friday.

item.title: Flight Canceled During the FAA Ground Stop? Here’s What to Do.
item.description: Travelers are entitled to refunds if their flights are canceled, regardless of the reason, but airlines won’t guarantee other amenities, such as a hotel room or meal vouchers.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chung
item.media:description: Travelers at Ronald Reagan National Airport in Washington on Friday.

item.title: Nvidia Scandal Prompts Questions of What It Means to Be a Spy
item.description: U.S. intelligence agencies believe a woman who had an affair with Jensen Huang was a Chinese asset. But there is much more that they are still assessing about her role.
item.dc:creator: Julian E. Barnes, Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan
item.category: Ministry of State Security of the People's Republic of China
item.media:description: There remains much that intelligence agencies are assessing about Alice Huang, whose relationship with Jensen Huang has come under intense scrutiny.

item.title: Why Jensen Huang Was Essential to Nvidia’s Rise
item.description: Jensen Huang was the driving force at Nvidia, with 60 direct reports and no clear succession plan. Tripp Mickle, one of our technology reporters, examines Mr. Huang’s central role in the company and the artificial intelligence industry.
item.dc:creator: Tripp Mickle, Gilad Thaler, Thomas Vollkommer, Shawn Paik, Nikolay Nikolov, James Surdam, Rafaela Balster, June Kim and Mark Oltmanns

item.title: Wall Street Loses a Powerful Dealmaker After Nvidia’s CEO Is Ousted
item.description: The ousted Nvidia chief executive was the consummate dealmaker leading the trillion-dollar A.I. build out.
item.dc:creator: Maureen Farrell and Rob Copeland
item.media:description: Some Wall Street bankers, traders and even some of Nvidia’s competitors are wondering and worrying about whether Jensen Huang’s departure will slow the breakneck pace of Nvidia’s investments.

item.title: Jensen Huang’s Leather Jacket Isn’t Helping Him Right Now
item.description: The Nvidia founder’s signature look branded him as a maverick. Does that image read differently now?
item.dc:creator: Jacob Gallagher
item.media:description: Jensen Huang’s jackets were a sly power move that helped him build his personal image and his Silicon Valley juggernaut.

item.title: Alaska Senate Race Between Dan Sullivan and Mary Peltola Still Counting Votes
item.description: The race between Senator Dan S. Sullivan and Ms. Peltola, a former congresswoman, is the only Senate contest that hasn’t been called.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Erin Schaff/The New York Times; Justin Sullivan/Getty Images
item.media:description: Former Representative Mary Peltola and Senator Dan S. Sullivan.

item.title: A Democrat Wins the Alaska Governor’s Race for the First Time Since 1998
item.description: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins made a name for himself as a coalition builder willing to raise alarms about his state’s dire fiscal straits.
item.dc:creator: Anna Griffin
item.media:description: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins at a coffee shop in Fairbanks, Alaska, in July.

item.title: Lauren Boebert Loses Re-election Bid in Colorado House Race to Eileen Laubacher
item.description: Ms. Boebert’s loss to Eileen Laubacher in a conservative House district represents a significant victory for Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner and Kellen Browning
item.media:description: Representative Lauren Boebert, a Republican from Colorado, was seen as increasingly vulnerable as her alliance with President Trump became a liability.

item.title: Did the Redistricting Wars Backfire on Republicans? In a Word, No.
item.description: The G.O.P. was able to avoid more House midterm losses — on top of the advantage it already had from gerrymandering.
item.dc:creator: Nate Cohn and Eve Washington

item.title: Developer Avoided Stricter Oversight Before Fatal Building Collapse
item.description: By winning approval for a three-story building, then seeking to add more stories, the Brooklyn developer was not subject to the more rigorous oversight required for larger projects.
item.dc:creator: Stefanos Chen, Mihir Zaveri, Amy Julia Harris, Bianca Pallaro, Dionne Searcey and William K. Rashbaum
item.media:credit: Dave Sanders for The New York Times
item.media:description: A site on Bedford Avenue in Brooklyn was under construction when a neighboring building collapsed.

item.title: Book Review: ‘Promise Me, America,’ by Joe Biden
item.description: The former president’s new memoir trumpets his achievements while justifying his decision to run for a second term and his embrace of Israel’s war in Gaza.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Szalai
item.media:description: Joe Biden’s memoir runs on two tracks: steady pragmatism and accelerating grandiosity.

item.title: 5 Takeaways from Joe Biden’s Memoir: The Debate, Dropping Out and Advice From Romney
item.description: The 46th president defends his decision to run for re-election, which many in his party now regard as a mistake, and revisits the disastrous debate that forced him to end his campaign.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Alyssa Schukar for The New York Times
item.media:description: Former President Joseph R. Biden writes in his memoir that he felt he had a handle on the challenges facing him before he dropped out of his run for re-election.

item.title: Jewish Heirs Challenge Sale of $180 Million van Gogh Painting at Sotheby’s
item.description: Heirs say “Blossoming Chestnut Trees” was sold under Nazi-era duress. The auction house says it is “committed to working toward a mutually satisfactory resolution.”
item.dc:creator: Catherine Hickley
item.media:description: Vincent van Gogh’s “Châtaigniers en Fleurs” was set to be the centerpiece of Sotheby’s auction next week.

item.title: All Accounted for After Tanker Crashes Into Docked New Orleans Riverboat
item.description: Gov. Jeff Landry of Louisiana called it a “literal miracle on the Mississippi” that all of the nearly 200 people aboard the riverboat were rescued.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Chao, Ishani Desai, Neil Vigdor and Shannon Sims

item.title: A ‘Generational Clash’ Is Fueling Europe’s Protests
item.description: As retirees live longer, governments need to spend more on pensions. That makes it harder to fund other services, spurring protests like those planned this weekend in France.
item.dc:creator: Jason Horowitz
item.media:credit: Julien De Rosa/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Students protesting last month in Paris. France is struggling to maintain both its education sector and its pension payments.

item.title: Trump to Meet With Putin and Xi in China, With Nuclear Proliferation on the Agenda
item.description: The president plans to also discuss the war against Iran, but is not expected to bring up Russia’s war in Ukraine or the scandal that has engulfed Jensen Huang.
item.dc:creator: Katie Rogers
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
Arms Control and Limitation and Disarmament
item.media:description: President Trump will meet jointly with Xi Jinping, China’s leader, and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia during a summit in China next week.

item.title: Inside Microsoft’s Rush to Get Back Online After a Global Outage
item.description: A prolonged outage left many without email and other services, the most recent reminder that the world’s technological underpinnings rely on just a few companies.
item.dc:creator: Karen Weise
item.media:credit: Grant Hindsley for The New York Times
item.media:description: Microsoft acknowledged that about 20 different services were impaired by the outage.

item.title: Microsoft’s Global Outage and Fixes: What We Know
item.description: The company described “encouraging” progress on efforts to overcome a second day of disruptions to its email, messaging and other services.
item.dc:creator: Michael Levenson
item.media:description: Microsoft said it was working to repair its services after a global outage that began on Thursday.

item.title: Russia Revives Demand That NATO Retrench to Secure Ukraine Deal
item.description: The hard-line position of Russian officials in closed-door negotiations about ending the war thrusts European security into the heart of the talks.
item.dc:creator: Anton Troianovski, Andrew E. Kramer, Jeanna Smialek, David E. Sanger and Eric Schmitt
item.media:description: Steve Witkoff, center left, and Jared Kushner, the U.S. envoys, with Kirill Dmitriev of Russia, right, in Moscow on Thursday.

item.title: Hakeem Jeffries Pushes to Lock Down House Speakership, With No Challenger Emerging
item.description: Facing resistance from the left but no challenger, the Democratic leader is sewing up support from key coalitions as his allies say he deserves a unanimous vote.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.media:description: Representative Hakeem Jeffries at the Capitol on Thursday.

item.title: Democrats Vie for Support in Race for Top Senate Job
item.description: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said he wouldn’t run for president to focus on his leadership challenge to Senator Chuck Schumer, who remained confident he would prevail.
item.dc:creator: Carl Hulse
item.media:credit: Daniele Volpe para The New York Times
item.media:description: Chris Van Hollen se había perfilado como el favorito para desafiar a Chuck Schumer por el puesto y en los últimos días había expresado una creciente disposición a hacerlo.

item.title: Trump Officials Press Congress to Renew Spying Law in Lame-Duck Session
item.description: The request to extend a high-profile warrantless surveillance law would add a thorny issue during waning Republican control.

item.media:description: In a letter to congressional leaders, three top national security officials in the Trump administration said the president was urging them to extend a surveillance law.
